work_packages.title: Prove both native representation relations.

evidence.claim: Source-bound specification of the Chez 10.3.0 tarm64le object representation for every Shen value kind, plus TC/frame/argument registers; SBCL 2.6.8 arm64 representation relations (KLValue and the CL-model sv values) with the E2E-21 host operations discharged against the captured inline type-test code; open items with owners. Exit criterion unmet.

Generated by scripts/package-repr-layout.py from pinned cmacros.ss/arm64.ss/arm64.def/types.h (tag v10.3.0 adfaf9e6) and the build-time tarm64le equates.h/machine.def; regenerated and diffed by scripts/prove. ChezRepr.chez_sources_agree, chez_object_layout, chez_register_layout and ChezWord.chez_fixnum_layout check cross-source agreement by computation.

Fixnum encode/decode round trip and injectivity on [-2^60, 2^60-1]; every tag-0 word is a fixnum; (fx x + fx y) mod 2^64 = fx (x+y); for fixnums, signed 64-bit addition of their words does not overflow iff x+y is a fixnum; (a|b)&7=0 iff both fixnum-tagged. Closed (rocq/Audit_Repr.v).

Representation relation rv between KLValue values and words over one byte-memory snapshot and a vector-location map; total tag decoder agreeing with rv; kind uniqueness; pointer/immediate/fixnum disjointness; void/unbound/eof/bwp/GC markers represent no value; decoding is a function on first-order data given injective locations; aligned fields; car/cdr, string-ref/length, vector-ref/length read the abstract components; shen_int_add_fast_path. Closures, ports and conditions are related only by shape plus meaning parameters (E2E-22/27/17). Closed.

Checked by ports/arm/islaris/check-islaris-shen.sh in the separate Coq 8.19.0 Islaris environment (not scripts/prove), compiling the same rocq/ChezLayout.v and rocq/ChezWord.v: for Shen integers x, y with x, y, x+y fixnums in X0/X1, X23=2 and the X20 frame slot, the captured Chez fast path returns X23 = fixnum word of x+y; the (a|b)&7=0 and no-overflow premises of buri_chez_add_fast_path are discharged. Closed. Still assumes EL2/MMU-off, the Armv8.5 isla traces, the base address, the X20 premises and the continuation.
One qemu-aarch64 run of the built tarm64le scheme: object words and pointer residues equal the encodings (ChezRepr.chez_sample_agrees). A sample, not evidence for the relation.

SBCL 2.6.8 arm64 layout: lowtags/widetags evaluated from pinned early-objdef.lisp under the image's features, registers from arm64/vm.lisp, equal to the constants captured from the pinned aarch64 image; layout facts (1-bit fixnum tag, 4-bit lowtags, NIL list pointer, char-code-limit #x110000). The relation itself is in rocq/SbclValues.v and rocq/SbclHostOps.v.
Sampled on host Shen-Scheme v0.52: (intern "12") is the integer 12, not VSym "12" as rule_intern prescribes (OB-SCHEME-INTERN-NUMERIC).

Generated by scripts/package-sbcl-type-tests.py (regenerated and diffed by scripts/prove) from the image capture ports/repr/sbcl/sbcl-2.6.8-arm64-type-tests.capture (raw 32-bit instruction words read from the code objects the pinned aarch64 SBCL 2.6.8 compiles for (lambda (x) (op x)), qemu-aarch64) and from the pinned SBCL sources arm64/type-vops.lisp, arm64/pred.lisp, generic/type-vops.lisp, type-vop-macros.lisp, genesis.lisp. SbclTests.frame_ground, full_calls, sbcl_source_flags, header_widetags_source and tests_match_sources check by computation the entry/return frame of each function, that STRING=/EQUAL/EQL/= are tail calls, and that each captured header test agrees with the define-type-vop type codes on every header widetag. The capture of the emitted code for an untyped argument is one compile run (sampled provenance); the checks on it are ground.

SBCL arm64 fixnums: one tag bit, encode/decode round trip and injectivity on [-2^62, 2^62-1]; every even word is a fixnum; tagged addition wraps; signed 64-bit addition of fixnum words does not overflow iff the sum is a fixnum; (a|b)&1=0 iff both are fixnums; slot alignment. Closed (rocq/Audit_Sbclnative.v).

For every register file (argument word in the register the window reads, NIL in the NULL register) and every memory, the decoded captured windows of EQ, TYPEP FIXNUM, INTEGERP, NUMBERP, CONSP, STRINGP, ARRAYP, SYMBOLP, NOT and NULL reach their end with R0 = T or NIL exactly as the word-level tests t_* say (SbclTests.*_window). Relative to the A64 decoder/semantics transcription in rocq/SbclA64.v (trust boundary), the captured untyped variants only (typed variants not covered), and the calling convention (frames, E2E-22). Closed.

Representation relation kv between KLValue values and SBCL words over one memory snapshot, a vector-location map and an interned-symbol table; NIL's list/symbol duality from genesis.lisp (nil_dual); on every represented value the captured tests compute kl_cons/kl_nil/kl_cl_symbol/... (kl_tests, kl_machine_tests): SYMBOLP is true on Shen [] and both Shen booleans; Shen false is CL true (kl_false_is_cl_true); VBool b and VSym of its name share a word (kl_bool_symbol_collision), so the relation is not a function on words; immediate/pointer disjointness; car/cdr and vector-ref read the components. Closed.

Relation cv between the CL-model values sv and SBCL words in a well-formed snapshot (injective interning, object identity and float spellings; T at NIL+56; genesis NIL layout); cv is a function on words (cv_functional); for every represented argument the captured code returns the representation of the cl_host_ops answer for CONSP, NULL, NOT, SYMBOLP, STRINGP, NUMBERP, INTEGERP, TYPEP FIXNUM and ARRAYP (e2e21_machine), and EQ's word comparison is sound and complete on symbols/NIL (eq_machine). A well-formed snapshot exists (ex_snap_wf). Closed.

work_packages.title: Close Chez compilation to ARM.

evidence.claim: Inventory of the Chez 10.3.0 tarm64le eval/compile pipeline actually run for Shen-Scheme v0.52 parameters (front end, 40 nanopass passes, 13 register-allocator sub-passes run per lambda, conditional passes), per-pass difficulty classes, effort estimate and the bridge to the E2E-20 ARM theorems. Exit criterion unmet.
Machine-readable pass inventory with source line ranges, languages, conditions and whether each ran for the captured function. Reading aid; the trace order is re-derived in Rocq.

Every traced pass output of real Chez 10.3.0 tarm64le (qemu-user) compiling the exact Shen-Scheme output of buri-arm-add with Shen-Scheme parameters; reproducible byte for byte (ports/chez-np/scripts/run-np-dump.sh); hash-pinned, packaged and diffed by make prove.
The x86_64 ta6le trace equals the tarm64le trace for the front end and the first 18 nanopass outputs and first differs at $np-expand-primitives. One function; not a machine-independence theorem.

np_languages_resolved: Rocq reads the 28 define-language forms of the pinned np-languages.ss, resolves every extends delta and obtains exactly the grammars behind the generated inductive syntax rocq/ChezNpSyntax.v (audited in rocq/Audit_Nanopass.v).

check_recognize_mrvs_sound: for all printed L4/L4.5 terms, acceptance implies equal core denotation and equal results under every primitive semantics, world type, truthiness and argument-evaluation-order policy; info fields the unparser omits are outside the semantics.

check_code_object_sound: acceptance implies the captured bytes are the np-generate-code template with each relocation window rewritten by arm64_set_abs, template windows hold item 0, and relocation offsets/targets equal the code object table.

For kl:buri-arm-add only: np-recognize-mrvs validated; 10 same-language passes print identically; the 152 captured tarm64le bytes are the relocation instance of np-generate-code output (codegen_buri_arm_add_instance); tampering rejected. Not a theorem about other programs.

Raw, info-carrying trace of the same compilation from Chez 10.3.0 with the printing-only patch ports/chez-np/patches/np-trace-raw.patch (trusted dumping tool, OB-CHEZ-NP-RAW-DUMP). Rerun byte-identical on the same boot files; a fresh patched build reproduces it except the block record-type uid.

With BURI_NP_RAW unset, the patched build's dump equals the stock capture except the block record-type uid, exactly as an unpatched rebuild does. One function; not a proof that the patch changes printing only.

check_raw_sound: raw L4/L4.5 terms read with their info-call and info-lambda fields (check? #f only on primref operators, no attachment shifting, interface* = clause interfaces); acceptance implies equal results under every primitive semantics, world, truthiness and order policy.

check_expand_plus_sound: for every L7 + call and L9 term the validator accepts, equal value and world under any primitive/library semantics meeting H_fix and H_lib (OB-CHEZ-LIB-PLUS), over a stated word-level semantics of the fixnum fast path (log!test tag check, +/ovfl, overflow condition code, label/goto fallback to library +). plus_expansion_fast needs no premise on primitives.
check_block_order_sound: accepted L16 pairs differ only in block-list order (sort_refs_perm), so every order-independent L16 meaning agrees. Says nothing about np-generate-code layout.

For kl:buri-arm-add only: $np-expand-primitives validated (expand_plus_buri_arm_add_preserves); the L9 fast path yields ChezWord.fx_enc (x + y) (expanded_fast_path_shen), the value buri_chez_add_shen proves at the byte level; np-suppress-procedure-checks validated with info fields; np-optimize-block-order! validated; 5 mutants rejected (audited in rocq/Audit_Chezprim.v).

work_packages.acceptance:
every required code
path/configuration is handled, or a universal compiler proof supplies the result.
A validator may reject an output safely, but cannot then claim universal coverage
of that unsupported required output. Generic closure uses compositional schemas,
not a test corpus. Proving outputs does not claim all unrelated Chez programs or
all possible compiler invocations are correct.

work_packages.title: Close SBCL compilation to ARM.
work_packages.acceptance:
the SBCL execution path has
the same coverage standard as Chez, without treating SBCL as a trusted oracle.

work_packages.title: Verify native runtime code and support libraries.
work_packages.acceptance:
no opaque native call remains in a required path. Replacing a dependency
with smaller code requires a proved API refinement and an explicit version change.

work_packages.title: Verify allocation and garbage collection.
work_packages.acceptance:
successful collections and all modeled failure paths preserve the runtime
invariant; there is no implicit “GC works” premise.

work_packages.title: Verify the executable lifecycle and exact loaded bytes.
work_packages.acceptance:
no gap remains between proved binary contents and modeled loaded code;
secure boot/physical identity roots are separately recorded in 31–32.

work_packages.title: Prove OS/ABI and IO boundary implementations.
work_packages.acceptance:
every interaction is explicit and wrapper correctness is discharged.
The remaining OS implementation relations are mandatory inputs to step 31,
not a declaration that the whole deployment is finished.

work_packages.title: Close concurrency, scheduling and ARM weak memory.
work_packages.acceptance:
all admitted interleavings and actual
runtime threads are covered; a sequential test cannot close this package.

work_packages.title: Connect TLA+ and distributed behavior.
work_packages.acceptance:
safety and conditional liveness are proved under
the exact fault/environment model; arbitrary permanent partition or hardware
failure is not hidden behind an unconditional availability claim.

work_packages.title: Prove security and resource claims separately.
work_packages.acceptance:
each
advertised guarantee has the right theorem, with environmental liveness and
physical side-channel assumptions exposed. No claim of universal termination.

work_packages.title: Close the deployment software below the process.
work_packages.acceptance:
no required software component is an unproved OS oracle.
Existing kernel proofs must be bridged into the checking trust story; assumptions
about unverified configurations, assembly or initialization are not inherited
silently. Hardware/device behavior remains an explicit physical foundation.

work_packages.title: Close checker execution and bootstrap trust.
work_packages.acceptance:
neither Shen execution nor an unproved extraction/compiler silently
decides theorem validity in the final acceptance route.

work_packages.title: Prove complete application examples on both ports.
work_packages.acceptance:
each example is end to end; finite examples demonstrate integration, while the
generic language/compiler results establish coverage beyond those examples.
Future applications still require their own contracts and certificates.

work_packages.title: Prove the composition theorem and close every premise.
work_packages.acceptance:
zero unproved software premises outside the declared ultimate checking root for
the closed endpoint and
zero required coverage holes. Unsupported output safely rejected by a validator
remains a coverage failure until its required case is implemented and proved.

work_packages.title: Make closure enforceable in CI and deployment.

evidence.claim: build manifests bind source, tool-payload, runtime-library, flag and proof-object hashes; not yet a signed bundle or deploy-time admission protocol

work_packages.acceptance:
modifying
any correctness-relevant input invalidates the old proof bundle, and no mutable
label or forgeable success token authorizes execution. Nix/Earthbuild repeatability
and signed provenance support this process but do not replace semantic checks.

work_packages.title: Perform independent closure review and release.
work_packages.acceptance:
every mandatory package
has its acceptance evidence and the final theorem applies to the bytes deployed.
Subsequent upgrades reopen affected obligations automatically. The release can
be complete even though future programs, platforms and hardware require new work.

work_packages.title: Freeze the Shen/JIT named build, profile and bytecode semantics.
work_packages.acceptance: the named build, its exclusions, trusted base and input boundary are written; a Rocq profile and executable bytecode semantics exist with stated metatheory; every deviation and open issue has a ledger entry; each gap in the shared KLambda semantics is resolved by a reviewed change or named as a limit of the claim.

work_packages.title: Prove KLambda to bytecode preservation for the actual Shen/JIT lowerer.
work_packages.acceptance: a universally quantified preservation theorem for a source-linked model of src/lowerer/lower.shen, plus validation of the exact stage 0 files against kernel KLambda.

work_packages.title: Prove bytecode to machine code for the Shen/JIT emitter.
work_packages.acceptance: for every bytecode object the build accepts, the code that runs simulates its bytecode under a value, heap and frame relation, by proving the emitter or a checker of its output, chosen from the measured emitter spike.

work_packages.title: Prove the Shen/JIT runtime on the exact binary.
work_packages.acceptance: function contracts on the exact binary for the collector, primitives, loader, errors and streams, with every premise discharged or named.

work_packages.title: Compose the Shen/JIT theorem and close the Shen frontend on it.
work_packages.acceptance: one theorem from the exact binary and its image, under the process model, to the KLambda semantics, with the input boundary stated, then connected to Shen source through the shared frontend packages.
